question: Do the museum and Codices Fennici records visibly depict the same fragment rather than merely repeat one description?

source_access.scope: Public IIIF viewer, whole displayed face; viewed in browser without saving a source image or cropping a derivative.
source_access.rights: CC BY-ND 4.0 on the CF record; reproduction Mikko Kyynäräinen / Turun Museokeskus.

source_access.scope: Public IIIF viewer, whole displayed face; later zoomed locally in the viewer. Filename labels are institutional, not a verified medieval side map.
source_access.rights: CC BY-ND 4.0 on the CF record; reproduction Mikko Kyynäräinen / Turun Museokeskus.

source_access.scope: Public museum record TKM23245:3 overview and its embedded thumbnail, viewed in browser. No failed TIFF link was retried.
source_access.rights: Museum record displays CC BY 4.0 with photographer or institution attribution.

matching_features: A large red O sits in the right text panel in both views.
Both views show the same uneven left and upper contours, central fold and relative arrangement of musical/text blocks.
visual_comparison.interpretation: The record thumbnails visibly depict the same face or a very close reproduction of it, strengthening the crosswalk between catalogue records beyond duplicated metadata.
visual_comparison.dependence: The images may be the same photograph or derived from a common source; this is not independent evidence of a manuscript-to-manuscript join. Low-resolution museum overview and possible cataloguing/image attachment errors limit certainty.

two_faces: The two CF viewer captures show a broad parchment fragment with two writing fields separated by a central fold. On the first displayed face the red O is on the right; on the other a large blue initial appears in the right field and a faint later account inscription is visible below it. This is consistent with the TEI's damaged bifolium and reported reuse; precise medieval recto/verso and quire position are not independently established.
record_crosswalk: Museum TKM23245:3 and CF item 249 are very strongly supported as records depicting the same fragment, without claiming certified object identity or resolving the separately named archive Ms. c.
sewing_holes: Marks near the central fold are visible, but none was measured or matched to a Finnish original. Published sewing-hole and placement claims remain untested.
article_route: The official journal.fi/htf/issue/archive page returned an Anubis challenge on one normal page open. Stopped without reload, interaction or bypass; the 2008 article page remains unread.
browser_view_transfer_bytes: unmeasured; image tiles displayed through the ordinary viewer
